title_en: Revised Thesis-Related Degree Requirements for Graduate Programs, from Fall 2026
summary: All graduate students in the master's, doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral programs who are examination candidates from Fall 2026 (September 2026) onward must meet the revised publication requirements for degree conferral. Proof of publication or acceptance must be issued, and any required signed confirmation for abstract-only conferences must be submitted, before the thesis examination results document submission date of the examination semester. Students must also check the Academic Handbook, as all other degree requirements remain unchanged.
applies_to: All graduate students in the master's, doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral programs who are thesis examination candidates from Fall 2026 (from September 2026) onward. Meeting these requirements is mandatory for degree conferral.

conditions: Master's: you must be the first author, excluding your supervisor, of at least one published (or accepted) domestic or international conference paper or journal paper, and your supervisor must be a co-author.
Master's: documents proving only journal submission are no longer accepted; the previous guideline accepting them has been abolished.
Master's: a paper on which you are a co-first author is not accepted, even if your name appears first.
Doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral: you must satisfy both Item (1) and Item (2).
Item (1): at least one paper published or accepted in an internationally recognised (SCI(E)-level) journal.
Item (2): at least one international conference paper or domestic journal paper published or accepted, or at least one registered international patent.
Doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral: only papers or patents that list your supervisor as a co-author and you as the first author excluding your supervisor are accepted.
Proof of publication or acceptance issued after the thesis examination results document submission date is not accepted.
Abstract-only conference papers are accepted only if the conference has a peer review process and the paper is confirmed by the signature of a preliminary examination committee member.
The signature may be obtained after the preliminary examination, provided it is submitted before the results document submission date.
Conference acceptance rate is not used as a criterion.
All other degree requirements not covered in this notice remain unchanged and must still be met.
The abstract-only conference criteria are new and may be revised through updates to this notice.
Final recognition is decided by your department; requirements may still not be recognised depending on detailed rules or individual circumstances.
steps: Read the Academic Handbook and the related notices linked in the original notice (graduate school must-read notice, thesis examination notice, list of conferences recognised as SCI(E)-level for doctoral requirements, and co-first author notice).
Check that your publications meet the requirements for your program, including authorship order and your supervisor's co-authorship.
If anything is ambiguous, email the department office before submitting your publication record; the contact is in the original notice.

For abstract-only conference papers: have a preliminary examination committee member sign a confirmation for the paper, presumably using the attached form 'Abstract-Submission Conference Record Confirmation' (초록 제출 학술대회 실적 확인서.hwp; its content was not read), and submit it before the thesis examination results document submission date.
Submit proof of publication or acceptance (publication record, acceptance email, etc.) that is issued before the thesis examination results document submission date of your examination semester.

Notice of Revised Degree Conferral (Thesis-Related) Rules for the Graduate School (Master's, Doctoral and Integrated Master's-Doctoral Programs)

We announce below the revised internal rules on degree conferral (thesis-related) for all graduate programs (master's, doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral). (Decided by the Academic Committee on Thursday 26 February 2026; detailed criteria added by the Academic Committee on Monday 10 August 2026.)

Effective: from September 2026 (from Fall 2026 examination candidates onward)

The following is an excerpt of the thesis-related rules in the Academic Handbook. All other degree conferral requirements not included here remain unchanged and must be met as before. Please be sure to check the Academic Handbook as well.

1. Publication requirements for degree conferral

A. Master's
Publish (or have accepted) at least one domestic or international conference paper or one journal paper on which your name appears first among the authors, excluding your supervisor. Your supervisor must be included as a co-author of the paper.
- Documents proving journal submission are not accepted even if submitted (the previous guideline accepting them is abolished).
- Even if your name appears first, the paper is not accepted if you are a co-first author.

B. Doctoral and integrated master's-doctoral
You must satisfy both Item (1) and Item (2) below. Only papers or patents that include your supervisor as a co-author and list your name first among the authors, excluding your supervisor, are accepted.
- (Item 1) At least one paper published or accepted in an internationally recognised journal (SCI(E) level).
- (Item 2) At least one international conference paper or domestic journal paper published or accepted, or at least one registered international patent.

C. Supporting documents (common to master's and doctoral)
Documents proving publication or acceptance (publication record, acceptance email, etc.) must be documents that can be issued before the thesis examination results document submission date of the examination semester. Documents issued after the results document submission date are not accepted as a publication record.

2. Detailed criteria for recognising conference records

Conferences requiring only an abstract
Conferences where only an abstract, not a full paper, is submitted may also be recognised if the following requirements are met.
- Recognition criterion: the conference must have a peer review process.
- Verification method: obtain the signature (confirmation) of a preliminary examination committee member for the record and submit it.
- Submission deadline: submit before the thesis examination results document submission date.
The signature may be obtained after the preliminary examination; it only needs to be submitted within the above deadline.
The acceptance rate is not applied as a recognition criterion.

3. Notes

The detailed criteria in Section 2 above were newly set by the Academic Committee on 10 August 2026. If parts needing improvement are identified during operation, revisions may be announced through this notice after review by the department office.

For anything ambiguous or difficult to judge, please be sure to contact the department office before submitting your publication record.

The exact rules and the final decision on whether requirements are met (recognised) follow the judgement (criteria) of your department. Please note in advance that, even if you meet the above, there may be cases where requirements are not recognised depending on detailed rules or individual circumstances.

4. Please also check

Graduate School must-read notice: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=56747
Thesis examination notice: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=56884
List of conferences recognised as international journal (SCI(E)) level for doctoral degree requirements: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=52081
Notice on co-first authorship: https://ece.snu.ac.kr/community/academics?md=v&bbsidx=55998

Inquiries: please email the department office; replies are sent in order. The contact details are in the original notice.
